Nadia Brennan-Aziz
Manchester, UK | nadia.brennanaziz@example.com | +44 7700 900909 | github.com/nba-sre-example

Dear Corvale Mobility Hiring Team,

I am applying for the Cloud Infrastructure / DevOps Contractor – Fleet Connectivity role. I bring 10 years of infrastructure experience, including six years operating Kubernetes platforms on AWS, and a track record of shaping reliable cloud platforms from design through production. Corvale’s plans to connect its new train fleet with cloud services make this an especially compelling opportunity to apply that experience to a new, end-to-end system.

At Tallybrook, I lead a five-person platform team operating eight AWS EKS clusters across three regions and approximately 350 services. I built an internal developer platform using service templates, Argo CD and Crossplane-based self-service provisioning, reducing the time to take a new service to production from around two weeks to under a day. I also introduced SLOs and error budgets for critical services, reducing weekly on-call pages by approximately 60%, and moved node provisioning to Karpenter with spot instances, reducing EC2 spend by 38%. These experiences have developed my ability to lead technical work, create practical infrastructure foundations, and help service teams build systems that are observable and operable.

My background also includes managing AWS infrastructure as code in Terraform across approximately 40 modules, using Atlantis for pull-request plan and apply workflows. I have operated systems at scale, replaced noisy monitoring with a Prometheus, Grafana, Alertmanager and Loki stack, and supported capacity planning for game launches serving up to 1.2 million daily active players. Alongside this, my experience with AWS networking and IAM, Linux operations, incident management and technical leadership gives me a strong foundation for contributing to Corvale’s secure and reliable train-to-cloud platform. I would bring an analytical, collaborative approach to system design and technical proposals, while working closely with backend teams and other stakeholders.

I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my platform engineering and AWS experience could support Corvale Mobility as it takes this fleet connectivity infrastructure from architecture to production. Thank you for your consideration.

Yours sincerely,
Nadia Brennan-Aziz

critique.content_quality_feedback: The cover letter is well structured, professional, concise, and supported by strong quantified evidence: team size, clusters, services, production lead time, on-call reduction, cost reduction, infrastructure modules, and user scale. The progression from platform leadership to broader infrastructure experience is logical. The main content weakness is that several claims are broad or aspirational rather than tied to demonstrated evidence, particularly system design, security, stakeholder alignment, and secure train-to-cloud communication. The letter also does not explicitly explain why the candidate's existing platform experience transfers to fleet connectivity beyond a general reference to Corvale's plans.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The document is highly parseable: it uses standard text, conventional headings, no tables or graphics, and clear contact details. It includes important terms such as AWS, EKS, Terraform, Kubernetes, infrastructure as code, IAM, Linux, observability, reliability, and technical leadership. However, AI/ATS screening probability is moderate to good rather than high because the letter does not contain several central job terms that the candidate's material does not substantiate, including Terragrunt, mTLS, SSL/TLS, certificate management, and train-to-cloud or remote-device integration. Those are candidate gaps rather than wording defects and should not be inserted without evidence. The letter could also use the exact supported term "cloud infrastructure design and operation" more directly and make the existing AWS VPC/IAM experience more visible.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The candidate is a strong match for hands-on AWS infrastructure operation, Kubernetes platforms, Terraform-based infrastructure as code, observability, reliability, Linux, and technical leadership. The scale and quantified results are particularly persuasive for a platform that must be reliable and operable. The candidate's experience also aligns with the company's engineering-led, ownership-oriented and collaborative culture, although the letter could connect those themes more explicitly to the evidence provided. The principal job-alignment gaps are Terragrunt, mutual TLS/SSL/TLS and certificate management, secure train-to-cloud communication, and IoT, automotive or remote-device integration. The material also does not establish a backend/JVM background. These are substantive experience gaps, not defects that can be solved by rewriting. Stakeholder alignment across external manufacturers is not demonstrated in the supplied candidate information.
critique.improvement_instructions:
CRITICAL: In the third paragraph, revise the sentence "Alongside this, my experience with AWS networking and IAM, Linux operations, incident management and technical leadership gives me a strong foundation for contributing to Corvale’s secure and reliable train-to-cloud platform." Do not present this as evidence of secure train-to-cloud communication, since the candidate information only supports AWS VPC/IAM and general operations. Change it to a precise supported statement such as: "Alongside this, my experience with AWS VPC and IAM, Linux operations, incident management and technical leadership gives me a strong foundation for contributing to the cloud infrastructure around Corvale’s train-to-cloud platform." 

CRITICAL: In the third paragraph, replace the unsupported or overly broad claim "while working closely with backend teams and other stakeholders." The original candidate information does not document collaboration with backend teams or external stakeholders. Use an evidence-based alternative such as "while helping product teams build services that are observable and operable," which is supported by the internal developer platform and observability experience.

MINOR: In the opening paragraph, replace the broad phrase "shaping reliable cloud platforms from design through production" with a more concrete supported formulation such as "designing, building and operating reliable AWS cloud platforms in production." This uses the job's language while staying grounded in the documented EKS, Terraform and platform-operation experience.

MINOR: In the second paragraph, make the job's system-design relevance more explicit without claiming unsupported train, IoT or certificate experience. After the sentence about the internal developer platform, add a short supported sentence such as: "This involved defining practical platform patterns, self-service interfaces and operational defaults that product teams could adopt consistently." This is grounded in the documented service templates, Crossplane provisioning and observable-service focus.

MINOR: In the final paragraph, replace "how my platform engineering and AWS experience could support Corvale Mobility as it takes this fleet connectivity infrastructure from architecture to production" with a more precise statement that does not imply prior fleet-connectivity experience: "how my platform engineering and AWS experience could support Corvale Mobility as it builds reliable, observable cloud infrastructure for its fleet connectivity services."
critique.critical_issues:
1. Potentially unsupported collaboration claim: the letter says the candidate will be "working closely with backend teams and other stakeholders," but the Original Candidate Information does not document this experience. Fix: replace that wording in the third paragraph with the supported product-team collaboration wording specified in improvement instructions.
2. Potentially overstated security/train-connectivity claim: the letter describes the candidate's AWS networking and IAM background as a foundation for a "secure and reliable train-to-cloud platform." The source material supports AWS VPC/IAM, but not mTLS, SSL/TLS, certificate management, or train-to-cloud systems. Fix: narrow the sentence to AWS VPC, IAM and cloud infrastructure contribution, as specified in improvement instructions.
Claims the sources (the candidate's own material; for the employer, the job ad and company research) do not support:
- “I would bring an analytical, collaborative approach”

Dear Corvale Mobility Hiring Team,

I am applying for the Cloud Infrastructure / DevOps Contractor – Fleet Connectivity role. I bring 10 years of infrastructure experience, including six years operating Kubernetes platforms on AWS, and a track record of designing, building and operating reliable AWS cloud platforms in production. Corvale’s plans to connect its new train fleet with cloud services make this an especially compelling opportunity to apply that experience to a new, end-to-end system.

At Tallybrook, I lead a five-person platform team operating eight AWS EKS clusters across three regions and approximately 350 services. I built an internal developer platform using service templates, Argo CD and Crossplane-based self-service provisioning, reducing the time to take a new service to production from around two weeks to under a day. This involved defining practical platform patterns, self-service interfaces and operational defaults that product teams could adopt consistently. I also introduced SLOs and error budgets for critical services, reducing weekly on-call pages by approximately 60%, and moved node provisioning to Karpenter with spot instances, reducing EC2 spend by 38%. These experiences have developed my ability to lead technical work, create practical infrastructure foundations, and help service teams build systems that are observable and operable.

My background also includes managing AWS infrastructure as code in Terraform across approximately 40 modules, using Atlantis for pull-request plan and apply workflows. I have operated systems at scale, replaced noisy monitoring with a Prometheus, Grafana, Alertmanager and Loki stack, and supported capacity planning for game launches serving up to 1.2 million daily active players. Alongside this, my experience with AWS VPC and IAM, Linux operations, incident management and technical leadership gives me a strong foundation for contributing to the cloud infrastructure around Corvale’s train-to-cloud platform. I would contribute to system design and technical proposals while helping product teams build services that are observable and operable.

I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my platform engineering and AWS experience could support Corvale Mobility as it builds reliable, observable cloud infrastructure for its fleet connectivity services. Thank you for your consideration.

Yours sincerely,
Nadia Brennan-Aziz

critique.content_quality_feedback: The cover letter is clear, professional, well structured, and appropriately tailored to Corvale Mobility's fleet-connectivity context. It leads with relevant experience, uses credible metrics, and demonstrates AWS, Kubernetes, platform engineering, infrastructure as code, observability, reliability, and technical leadership. The examples are specific and persuasive, particularly the reduction in service launch time, on-call pages, and EC2 spend. The main limitation is that some claims about system design and technical proposals are expressed as future contributions rather than supported examples from the candidate's background.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The letter is ATS-friendly: it uses a conventional layout, plain text headings and paragraphs, standard contact details, and searchable terms such as AWS, EKS, Kubernetes, Terraform, Atlantis, Argo CD, Crossplane, VPC, IAM, Linux, incident management, observability, reliability, and technical leadership. It should parse reliably and has a strong AI-screening profile for AWS/platform-engineering roles. Matching is weakened by the absence of Terragrunt, mTLS, SSL/TLS, certificate management, security, and remote-device/IoT terminology. These are genuine candidate-profile gaps where they are not supported by the Original Candidate Information, so they should not be inserted merely for keyword matching.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The document aligns strongly with the hands-on infrastructure, AWS, Terraform, cloud operations, observability, reliability, Linux, and technical-leadership aspects of the role. It also connects the candidate's experience to helping product teams build services that are observable and operable, which fits Corvale's end-to-end ownership model. The candidate's evidence is relevant to systems/platform design, although the letter could make that connection more concrete. The candidate material does not show Terragrunt, mTLS or SSL/TLS, certificate management, IoT/automotive/remote-device integration, or backend/full-stack/JVM experience; these are gaps rather than document defects. IAM and VPC provide some evidence of practical cloud security and networking awareness, but the specific secure train-to-cloud communication requirements are not demonstrated.
critique.improvement_instructions: Minor enhancement only: In the third paragraph, replace the sentence beginning "Alongside this, my experience with AWS VPC and IAM" with a more ATS-aligned, evidence-based sentence such as: "Alongside this, my hands-on experience with AWS VPC and IAM, Linux operations, infrastructure as code, incident management and technical leadership gives me a strong foundation in cloud environment design and operation, practical access-control decisions, and the delivery of observable, operable services." This makes the supported job terms "cloud environment design and operation" and "practical security" more explicit without claiming unsupported mTLS, SSL/TLS, certificate-management, or Terragrunt experience. Also, in the second paragraph, change "These experiences have developed my ability to lead technical work, create practical infrastructure foundations" to "These experiences demonstrate my ability to lead technical work and create practical infrastructure foundations" so the letter presents the documented evidence more directly rather than using a general capability statement.
